tool_input.command:
cat > .architect/decisions/ADR-0004-soft-delete-trash.md <<'EOF'
---
id: ADR-0004
title: Delete moves a task to a trash; restore brings it back
status: proposed
date: 2026-10-25
drivers: [CAP-003, QA-001]
---

## Context

CAP-003 said a task is deleted permanently, with a confirmation, and the blueprint listed "Undo, trash
and soft delete" as a non-goal. The owner has since asked for a safe way to recover a task deleted by
mistake. This ADR reverses that non-goal, for deletion only (undoing other edits stays out of scope).

## Decision

- `DELETE /api/tasks/:id` sets `tasks.deleted_at` (migration 002) instead of removing the row. It
  answers `204`, or `404` when the task is missing or already deleted.
- `GET /api/tasks` returns active tasks only. `GET /api/tasks/deleted` returns the trash, most
  recently deleted first, with `deleted_at`.
- `POST /api/tasks/:id/restore` clears `deleted_at` and answers `200 {"task"}`, or `404` when the
  task is not in the trash. The task keeps its id and timestamps.
- A malformed id answers `400 validation_failed`.
- The page asks no confirmation, because deleting is reversible: it lists "Recently deleted" tasks
  with a Restore button.
- Deleted rows are kept, in the same SQLite file and under the same durability pragmas (ADR-0002), so
  a delete or restore that was acknowledged survives `kill -9`.

## Rejected alternatives

- **Hard delete with a confirmation dialog.** A confirmation does not help once it is confirmed by
  habit; the data is gone.
- **A separate trash table.** Two writes to move a row, and a restore that must re-insert with the
  old id. A nullable column is one atomic `UPDATE`.

## Consequences

- The trash grows without limit: there is no way to empty it or to delete a task for good yet. For
  one person's task list this is small; an "empty trash" action or a retention period is a follow-up.
- Ids of deleted tasks are never reused (`AUTOINCREMENT`), so a restore cannot collide.
- Every query on `tasks` must filter on `deleted_at`; they all live in `src/tasks.ts`.
EOF
perl -0pi -e 's/\| DELETE \| `\/api\/tasks\/:id` \| Hard delete, `204` \|/| DELETE | `\/api\/tasks\/:id` | Move to the trash (soft delete), `204`; `404` when missing or already deleted |\n| GET | `\/api\/tasks\/deleted` | `200 {"tasks":[...]}`, the trash, most recently deleted first, each with `deleted_at` |\n| POST | `\/api\/tasks\/:id\/restore` | Take a task out of the trash, `200 {"task"}`; `404` when it is not in the trash |/; s/`not_found` as 404\./`not_found` as 404. A malformed task id in the path is `validation_failed`./; s/(- ADR-0003: architecture tests enforce the boundary rules\.)/$1\n- ADR-0004: delete moves a task to a trash, and restore brings it back./' .architect/architecture.md
perl -0pi -e 's/  - Undo, trash and soft delete\n/  - Undo of anything but a deletion, and emptying the trash (ADR-0004)\n/; s/The owner can rename a task, or delete it permanently with a confirmation\./The owner can rename a task, or delete it and restore it from the trash if it was a mistake (ADR-0004)./' .architect/blueprint.yaml
printf '| Deleted task | A task moved to the trash (`deleted_at` set). It is hidden from the list and can be restored. |\n| Trash | The deleted tasks, shown as "Recently deleted". Nothing empties it yet. |\n' >> .architect/glossary.md
git diff .architect | head -70

result:
Ya se pueden borrar tareas y recuperar las borradas por error. `npm test` pasa (31 de 31) y `npm run typecheck` no da errores. Todo está en un commit (`0c477d3`).

**Cómo funciona**
- **Borrar:** `DELETE /api/tasks/:id` ya no elimina la fila. La mueve a una papelera marcándola con `deleted_at` y responde `204`. Si la tarea no existe o ya estaba borrada, responde `404`.
- **Papelera:** `GET /api/tasks/deleted` lista las tareas borradas, la más reciente primero. `GET /api/tasks` solo devuelve las activas.
- **Recuperar:** `POST /api/tasks/:id/restore` devuelve la tarea con el mismo id y las mismas fechas. Si no está en la papelera, responde `404`.
- **Ids inválidos:** un id mal formado (`abc`, `-1`, `1.5`, un número enorme) responde `400 validation_failed` y no cambia nada.
- **Migración:** la migración `002` añade la columna `deleted_at`. Las bases creadas antes siguen abriendo, y hay un test que lo comprueba.
- **Página:** cada tarea tiene un botón "Delete" y aparece una sección "Recently deleted" con "Restore". No pide confirmación, porque borrar ya se puede deshacer. Si una acción falla, muestra un mensaje.
- **Tests:** `tests/delete-restore.test.ts` cubre todo lo anterior. También comprueba que un borrado y una restauración sobreviven a `kill -9` y reinicio.

**Un cambio en el diseño**
- `blueprint.yaml` tenía "Undo, trash and soft delete" como non-goal, y `architecture.md` describía un borrado definitivo. Seguí tu petición explícita y lo dejé documentado en `ADR-0004` (estado `proposed`). Actualicé también `architecture.md`, `blueprint.yaml` y el glosario. Si prefieres otro enfoque, dímelo.

**Lo que no cubre**
- **Papelera sin límite:** no hay forma de vaciarla ni borrar una tarea para siempre. Para una lista personal es poco, pero queda como siguiente paso (vaciar la papelera o un plazo de retención).
- **Guard Host/Origin:** `architecture.md` lo exige, pero aún no existe en el código. Mientras no esté, un sitio externo podría enviar `POST /restore` o `DELETE` a `localhost`.
- **Fuera de alcance, sin tocar:** `PATCH`, la validación del título y el manejo de JSON inválido en `POST /api/tasks`. Este último devuelve 500 hoy.
